title: Book One · Chapter 47: Dad's Clean Shirt
story:
Dad washes his best shirt in the evening. Mum points to the new thread at one cuff. It is pulling the cloth tight. She repairs that part. Dad hangs the rest of the shirt by the open window.

“Are you going somewhere?” Ronan asks.

“I am going to ask a man about regular work.”

“Like your old shop?”

“I want to work at his place. I am not opening my old shop again.”

Ronan looks at the blue toolbox. It is under the table, as always. Will Dad take it to the new shop? Will he leave it there? Ronan wants to know.

“Will your box still be yours?”

“Yes.”

“Will you come home?”

Dad turns from the shirt. “Yes. The job is in town. I will come home after work each day.”

Ronan nods. Ronan was afraid of a job far away. Now Dad is telling him about a job near home.

The next morning, Dad leaves after breakfast. A name is on the paper in his pocket: Mr Sun. Ronan wants to go, too. But he has school. Dad also needs to speak on his own.

All morning, Ronan thinks of a yellow sun. He imagines it on the shop wall. At break, he tells Leo. Leo laughs at the yellow sun. “Sun is the man's name,” he says. “He may not have a sun on his wall.”

“What does my name have?” Ronan asks.

“You write a very big R. That is your sign.”

That makes him laugh. He finds his place in the book again. He reads two lines. For a little while, he forgets Dad's shirt.

After school, Dad isn't home yet. Mum knows his expected time. She doesn't stand at the gate. Mum puts the finished trousers in a bag. Then she checks another hem.

“Does Dad have the job?” Ronan asks. A few minutes later, he asks again.

“I don't know,” she says each time.

Mum puts her needle down. “I cannot answer yet. We need Dad's news. You can help me count these buttons. Or read beside me.”

He chooses his reading book. On the page, a man waits at a gate. Ronan looks at the man in the picture. The man waits in the picture. Ronan waits at home, too. Ronan turns to the words and tries to read.

Dad comes back before dinner. His shirt is still clean except at one wrist.

“Mr Sun will think about it,” he says. “He needs to check his jobs for next week.”

“Did you fix something?” Ronan asks.

“He asked me to look at a loose hand crank. I found a possible problem. I pointed it out to him. He will check that part.”

“Why didn't you just do it?”

“It isn't my counter. Mr Sun needs to agree first.”

Mum asks about hours and pay. Dad tells her about the talk. They discussed some details. Some are still open. “What are the hours?” Mum asks. “And the pay?” Dad explains the possible hours and pay. He still needs a tool list. Mr Sun chooses the first repair, then the next one.

After dinner, Dad hangs the shirt on a hook. Now the shirt is ready for another visit. Mum gets the family notebook. She writes Mr Sun's name and address there. This is not her sewing list.

Ronan offers to draw the place on the map. “We can walk there together,” Dad says. “Then you can put it on the map.”

Before bed, Ronan asks one more question.

“Did he like you?”

Dad thinks a moment. “He listened to me.”

Ronan watches him fold the cuffs neatly. Ronan wants to hear more. Dad is quiet now. Dad hangs the clean shirt by the door. He can wear it for his next talk with Mr Sun. Ronan leaves it there.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：regular work＝固定工作；pay＝报酬；cuff＝袖口；counter＝柜台。

辅助理解：hand crank＝手摇柄；hem＝衣服折边；Sun在这里是人名。

理解问题：

1. Dad 为什么换上干净衬衣？
2. Ronan 从这次等待中知道了工作安排的哪些实际情况？
